projects.title: The Commons
projects.summary: A community-driven pickleball identity built around movement, connection and shared experiences.
projects.intro:
A community-driven pickleball identity built around movement, connection and shared experiences.

The visual language transforms the energy of the court into a playful world that extends beyond the game.

blocks.label: Role
blocks.heading: My Role
blocks.body: Developed the visual identity and graphic system for The Commons, translating the energy of pickleball into a playful and cohesive brand language across physical and digital touchpoints.
blocks.kicker: Brand Identity · Art Direction · Visual System · Applications

blocks.heading: The Context
blocks.body: The Commons is imagined as more than a place to play pickleball. It is a space built around bringing people together through play, movement and shared experiences. The challenge was to create an identity that could capture the energy of the sport while feeling social, approachable and distinctive.

blocks.heading: The Idea
blocks.body:
The identity is built around the idea of the court as a shared space. Its lines, shapes and geometry become the foundation of the visual language, translating the physical energy of pickleball into something playful, social and dynamic.

Court markings are abstracted into bold graphic forms, creating a visual system that can move between the game, the brand and the wider community.

blocks.title: Process
blocks.note: Logo, colour and the building blocks of the system.

blocks.heading: The Identity
blocks.body: A vibrant orange and layered purple palette gives the identity its energy, while rounded forms and compact typography keep it approachable. The system balances the competitive energy of sport with the relaxed, social character of a community space.

blocks.heading: The Visual System
blocks.body:
The visual system combines court-inspired geometry, bold colour blocks, playful graphics and photography. These elements can be rearranged across different formats while maintaining a consistent and recognisable brand presence.

Photography focuses on movement, interaction and the people around the game, reinforcing The Commons as a social space rather than simply a sports venue.

blocks.title: Final Deliverables
blocks.note: Signage, equipment, merchandise, café and social.

blocks.heading: The Applications
blocks.body: The identity extends across the physical and digital experience, from court signage and equipment to social communication and branded touchpoints. The same visual language keeps every part of the experience connected.

projects.title: 1000 Burgers
projects.summary: A bold identity for a focused gourmet burger concept built around the idea of quantity.
projects.intro:
A bold identity for a focused gourmet burger concept built around the idea of quantity.

The visual language turns “1000” into a playful graphic device, creating a brand that feels excessive, energetic and unmistakably burger-obsessed.

blocks.label: Role
blocks.heading: My Role
blocks.body: Developed the visual identity and graphic language for 1000 Burgers, translating the brand's idea of quantity into a bold and flexible system across packaging, communication and physical touchpoints.
blocks.kicker: Brand Identity · Art Direction · Packaging · Visual Applications

blocks.heading: The Context
blocks.body: 1000 Burgers is built around doing one thing exceptionally well: burgers. With a deliberately focused offering, the challenge was to create an identity that could make this singular focus feel expansive, playful and memorable.

blocks.heading: The Idea
blocks.body:
The name 1000 Burgers became the starting point for the identity. Rather than treating “1000” as simply a number, it became a visual expression of excess, repetition and an almost obsessive love for burgers.

The idea is pushed further through the transformation of the burger itself, compressing and morphing it into the “0” within 1000.

blocks.title: Process
blocks.note: From the burger-to-zero morph to the repeating numeral system.

blocks.heading: The Identity
blocks.body:
The identity uses bold typography, repetition and oversized graphic forms to create a visual language that feels abundant and unapologetic. The number 1000 becomes a recurring graphic device, allowing the brand to stay recognisable across different applications.

The system balances the playful idea of excess with a focused and confident visual character.

blocks.heading: The Visual System
blocks.body: Repetition became a key part of the visual language, extending the idea of quantity beyond the name. Burger-inspired graphics, stickers and modular compositions create a flexible system that can be scaled across packaging, merchandise and communication.

blocks.title: Final Deliverables
blocks.note: Packaging, stickers, merchandise and promotional graphics.

blocks.heading: The Applications
blocks.body: The identity was extended across packaging, stickers, physical brand touchpoints and promotional graphics, allowing the idea of 1000 to become part of the experience rather than simply a name.

projects.title: Silair
projects.summary: A premium sparkling water brand inspired by the landscapes and heritage of Rajasthan.
projects.intro:
A premium sparkling water brand inspired by the landscapes and heritage of Rajasthan.

Silair brings together purity, mindful luxury and regional storytelling through a distinctive identity, can system and product world.

blocks.label: Role
blocks.heading: My Role
blocks.body: Developed the brand concept and visual identity for Silair, translating its connection to Siliserh Lake and Rajasthan into a contemporary can system and product world. The project also involved packaging design and creating the final product visualisations.
blocks.kicker: Brand Strategy · Brand Identity · Packaging · Product Visualisation · Art Direction

blocks.heading: The Context
blocks.body: Premium sparkling water is a crowded shelf where most brands speak the same cool, minimal language. The opportunity was to give Silair a sense of origin — a brand that feels rooted in a real place while still belonging to a contemporary lifestyle.

blocks.heading: The Idea
blocks.body:
Silair takes its name and narrative from Siliserh Lake in Rajasthan, using the landscape as the foundation for the brand story. The identity interprets the region through flowing forms and ornamental details, connecting the natural source of the water with its cultural surroundings.

The aim was to create a sparkling water brand that feels rooted in place while still belonging to a contemporary premium lifestyle.

blocks.title: Process
blocks.note: Ideation sketches, illustration and the dieline.

blocks.heading: The Identity
blocks.body: An ornamental wordmark and hand-drawn swirls of fruit and water carry the story of the lake onto every can. Each flavour — peach, lime and blackberry — gets its own colour world, while the shared illustration style keeps the range unmistakably Silair.

blocks.title: Final Deliverables
blocks.note: The can system, multipacks and the 3D product world.

blocks.heading: The Packaging
blocks.body:
The can system translates the brand story into a bold, cohesive product family. Each flavour is given its own colour and graphic treatment, while the shared structure and visual language keep the range recognisably Silair.

The elongated can format and expressive graphics give the sparkling water a distinctive presence, balancing shelf impact with a more considered premium character.

blocks.heading: The Product World
blocks.body: Product visualisation became an extension of the brand identity, placing the cans within a carefully constructed world of colour, light and material. The renders explore Silair as both a refreshing product and a premium lifestyle object.

projects.title: Ibaco
projects.summary: Reimagining Ibaco as an ice cream destination inspired by flavours from around the world.
projects.intro:
Reimagining Ibaco as an ice cream destination inspired by flavours from around the world.

The identity turns its 36-flavour range into a visual journey through landmarks, illustrations and playful brand experiences.

heroCompare.hint: Hover to see the old logo

blocks.label: Role
blocks.heading: My Role
blocks.body: Collaborated on the rebranding of Ibaco, contributing to the visual identity, illustration system and packaging applications. I developed the landmark-based illustration concept that became a key part of the new brand language.
blocks.kicker: Brand Identity · Illustration · Packaging · Visual Direction

blocks.heading: The Context
blocks.body: Ibaco had a strong product offering, but its existing visual identity had become inconsistent across packaging, communication and digital touchpoints. The opportunity was to create a more contemporary and cohesive identity while retaining the variety that made the brand distinctive.

blocks.heading: The Idea
blocks.body:
Ibaco's 36 flavours take inspiration from different parts of the world. Rather than treating this variety as a list of products, the identity turns each flavour into a destination, pairing it with landmarks and visual references from its place of inspiration.

These illustrations became the foundation for a playful visual world that communicates Ibaco's global range while giving each flavour its own story.

blocks.title: Process
blocks.note: Landmark illustrations and the new wordmark.

blocks.heading: The Identity
blocks.body:
The new identity builds on the idea of discovery and destination. The dot above the “i” becomes a location pin, while the relationship between the “c” and “o” references an open mouth and a scoop of ice cream.

A refined wordmark and simplified visual language give the brand a more contemporary presence while keeping its playful character intact.

blocks.heading: The Visual System
blocks.body: The landmark illustrations were developed as a flexible visual library, allowing the identity to shift between flavours and applications while remaining recognisably Ibaco. A warm red, cream and chocolate palette gives the system a playful but grounded character.

blocks.title: Final Deliverables
blocks.note: Packaging, menus, merchandise, digital and spaces.

blocks.heading: The Applications
blocks.body: The system was extended across packaging, menus, digital experiences, merchandise and physical spaces, allowing the idea of an ice cream destination to exist beyond the product itself.

projects.title: Gender & Gesture
projects.summary: An event identity exploring the relationship between gender, gesture and visual expression.
projects.intro:
An event identity exploring the relationship between gender, gesture and visual expression.

A fragmented visual language uses movement, form and photography to challenge fixed ideas of identity and expression.

blocks.label: Role
blocks.heading: My Role
blocks.body: Developed the visual identity and event branding system, including the logo, typography, colour palette and promotional applications.
blocks.kicker: Event Branding · Visual Identity · Art Direction

blocks.heading: The Idea
blocks.body:
The identity explores gender as something fluid rather than fixed. A fragmented starburst form became the central visual device, representing movement, expression and the breaking of boundaries.

The logo draws from the segmented movement of a camera shutter, connecting photography with the idea of capturing fleeting gestures and different forms of identity.

blocks.title: Process
blocks.note: Sketches, the mark, type and colour.

blocks.heading: The Visual System
blocks.body:
The visual language combines fragmented typography, expressive graphic forms and a red and purple palette to create a system that feels energetic and intentionally disruptive.

Photography and abstract gestures become part of the identity, allowing the system to shift between structured layouts and more expressive compositions.

blocks.title: Final Deliverables
blocks.note: Exhibition graphics, passes, print and spatial applications.

blocks.heading: The Applications
blocks.body: The identity was extended across exhibition graphics, passes, promotional material and spatial applications, creating a cohesive visual environment for the event.

projects.title: Digital Sculpting
projects.summary: A digital sculpting study exploring organic forms, facial features and ornamental detail in ZBrush.
projects.intro:
A digital sculpting study exploring organic forms, facial features and ornamental detail in ZBrush.

Recreated from an existing sculpting reference as a first exploration into digital character sculpting.

blocks.label: Role
blocks.heading: My Role
blocks.body: Recreated the reference sculpture in ZBrush as a study in digital sculpting, focusing on facial structure, organic forms and sculptural detailing.

blocks.heading: The Study
blocks.body: The project began as an exercise in translating an existing sculpt into a 3D workflow. The focus was on understanding form, proportion and surface detail while developing familiarity with ZBrush's sculpting tools.

blocks.title: Process
blocks.note: Blocking out the face, refining features and building detail.

blocks.heading: The Sculpt
blocks.body: The final sculpt explores the original character's elongated forms, layered hair and ornamental details through my own reconstruction.

blocks.title: Final Deliverables
blocks.note: Final renders of the finished sculpt.

blocks.heading: The Result
blocks.body: A first exploration into digital sculpting, developed as a study of form, detail and the possibilities of working in ZBrush.
